newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse index rises on foreign demand.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse index rises on foreign demand.

text.p: Renewed foreign interest on selected key shares helped the Nairobi Stock Exchange 20-share index bounce back on Wednesday, bourse officials said.
The index gained 2.17 points to close at 3349.62.

Turnover, boosted by a deal on the one-hour special board for Kenya Commercial Bank, was posted at 29.551 million shillings on 509,601 shares compared to 19.469 million shillings on 339,706 shares on Tuesday.
Foreigners traded the bank's shares at a reserve price of 97 from 96. They also bought National Industrial Credit at 49.75 from 49.50 and Kenya Breweries at between 57 and 58 from 58.50.
Activity on the other boards was flat with the share prices fluctuating marginally.
Barclays Bank eased to 99 from 100 while Standard Chartered closed at 44.25 from 44.75.
Bamburi Cement closed at 40 from 39 while Total Kenya eased to 64 from 65.
Brokers said the movement of the index back and forth within a narrow range reflected a lack of clear direction: "We expect it to come down once all books close," a senior broker said.
Most companies have released their year-end results and will close their registers by end of May.
Meantime Kenya Oil Company announced a first and final dividend of four shillings per share.
The group said it made a profit of 95.1 million shillings ($1.7 million) after tax for the year ended September 30, 1996 compared to 84.2 million shillings in the previous year.
At the end of the day's trading session, the share stood at 65.50, untraded.
Some 25.63 million shillings of the floating rate treasury bonds were traded at between 100.8650 percent and 100.9123 percent compared to 100.6667 percent on Tuesday.
